content:
maria_sales: Quick heads-up — POC kickoff with Helix Capital today. They're seeing slow TTFT (~2s+) on short prompts and a weird throughput collapse around 45–60 RPS. They want us on a swarming call if possible to unblock.

ton y_se: can you paste an example request + payload size and what model variant they're hitting? also any logs or request IDs would help.

maria_sales: sending sample now. model: redwood-v1-medium; prompt len ~40 tokens; response expected ~20 tokens. Sample request_id: req_20240314_helix_01

maria_sales: log snippet they attached:
```
2024-03-14T15:02:12Z ERROR inference: request=req_20240314_helix_01 latency=2.32s first_token=2.31s total_tokens=22 backend=hosted-vm-23
2024-03-14T15:02:13Z WARN router: batching_delay=120ms batch_size=8 route=default
```

elaine_engruntime: thanks — two obvious suspects: 1) prefix/KV cache cold start for the particular prompt shape, 2) unintended batching that increases TTFT for single-client flows. Also need to check kernel selection logs and if quantized variant was chosen.

ben_support: also verify they're not hitting per-user concurrency limits which can drop throughput when many sessions hammer sequentially. any 429s in the logs?

maria_sales: Helix says no 429s, they saw a couple 504s earlier. Attach full perf trace: https://internal-traces/redwood/trace/abcd1234

elaine_engruntime: opening trace — I see long gap before first token for a couple of requests: the runtime waited ~1.9s in "queue" state then perf jump. Can you share their client-side concurrency pattern? Are they using client-side retries with backoff that causes bursts?

ton y_se: their test harness is a node script hitting endpoint with 50 concurrent clients, each doing 1 request every 2s. So steady 50 concurrency. That could push into batching window where batching tries to fill to 8/16 and waits 100–200ms; if requests align badly we get extra wait time on first token.

elaine_engruntime: try the following quick experiments for POC:
- set request header `x-redwood-batching: "disabled"` to force single-request dispatch (TTFT tradeoff vs throughput)
- set `max_batching_delay_ms=25` on their account for low-latency use-case
- enable prefix cache warmup by sending a pinned warmup prompt once per instance

ben_support: i'll message them the above steps and provide a small script to toggle header. also asking them to collect `X-Request-ID` from next 20 slow requests.

maria_sales: they tried `max_batching_delay_ms=25` and saw TTFT drop to ~600ms but throughput at 50 RPS dropped ~12%. They prefer latency over raw throughput for now — want guidance on config tradeoffs.

elaine_engruntime: that's expected. Options:
- use smaller batch windows (good for latency) but reduces token/sec efficiency
- enable per-customer dedicated capacity (Reserved) to get both latency and throughput guarantees
- enable KV/prefix caching aggressively and warm the cache (improves TTFT without batching penalties)

maria_sales: they asked about cost impact of dedicated capacity vs hosted tweaks — any rough numbers?

elaine_engruntime: ballpark: hosted w/ tight batching and cache tuning reduces unit cost ~10–30% vs default, but reserved capacity (1-2 GPUs sized for profile) increases infra cost but gives 2–3x consistent throughput per GPU and removes queuing jitter. I'll follow up with a short calc.

infra-bot: deploy v1.2.3 to hosted-cluster-1 scheduled at 2024-03-14T17:00Z (no restarts expected)

ton y_se: one more troubleshooting step: can you run a micro benchmark against the exact model/container from within their region? Command we usually send:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":20}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/models/redwood-v1-medium:predict -o /tmp/out && jq . /tmp/out
```

ben_support: got a few more logs from Helix — they show intermittent `batch_size=1` but lots of `batch_size=12` spikes. Also kernel_version shows fallback to generic kernel at times: `kernel=generic_fallback_2024-02-11` which explains jitter.

elaine_engruntime: ok that explains it — kernel fallback typically happens when sequence length distribution differs from compiled profile. Ask them to provide length histogram from tests (prompt+response length). If majority <128 tokens compile profile for that shape reduces fallback.

maria_sales: action items I captured for swarming call:
- Helix to attach 30 raw request_ids of slow requests
- Helix to provide prompt+response length histogram
- Helix to try `x-redwood-batching: disabled` and report TTFT/throughput
- Eng to propose short cost estimate for reserved capacity vs tuned hosted config
- Eng-runtime to check kernel selection logs for their tenant and, if needed, push compiled profile

ben_support: i'll set up a 30-min swarming session at 18:00 UTC and invite infra/eng-runtime. I'll also share a small JS helper to toggle header and collect ids.

maria_sales: perfect — Helix is aligned to join. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: canary rollout v1.2.3 -> hosted-cluster-1 succeeded for 3/5 nodes, monitoring for errors.

elaine_engruntime: post-swarm follow-up: if they opt for dedicated, we should include KV cache pinning and a precompile step for their common shapes. I'll draft a short doc with steps and cost table.

maria_sales: thanks — adding Helix to follow-up thread and will capture meeting notes.
